items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: They already had – JR had played drums, Paul Jackson Jr., Eric was going to come in and play the guitar. ... So I went in there and did my thing.

ctx.x: After you did like a couple of hundred studio dates I’m guessing that you stopped reporting on every one of them when you got home. I mean here in Central New York we don’t – if you do a studio date it’s sort of an event. And you come home and sort of say, “Hey how did it go.” What would really make you bring this up, what your date was like today to your wife or your kids. This was significant? What kind of date?

If I played on a song, if this is a record and I played on a song that I thought was really going to be a hit then I’d mention. I remember I played on an Eric Clapton song, it was called “Change the World” I think that was the name, “Change the World.” It was a hit. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

And I remember going in, and the producer was Babyface. And I went to overdub. They already had – JR had played drums, Paul Jackson Jr., Eric was going to come in and play the guitar. And here’s an example of a great producer. Babyface would come in, says, “Hey check it out. Listen to the song.” He goes, “You know what to do.” So I went in there and did my thing. But the song was so great, I came home and I went like, “I think I just played on a hit song.” Eric Clapton. Okay. And another time it was, this is a…
